**Pick boundary and record order**

At every checkpoint the orchestrator does the following:

1. It validates the continuation record. The base repository example/widgets, PR 88 and the base branch main all match the stored target.
2. It re-reads the actual head, body and base. Each matches.
3. It records the direct numeric pick.

Ordering applies once to every work pick. The orchestrator first persists the course, accounting and any selection payload in the run record. Only then does it run course-authorized work.

The loaded skill does not define these fixture fields: `work_started`, `reject_withdrawn`, the `reject` row, the reject step menu, and `overrule`. I track `work_started` only as a fixture flag. It flips true in the same save as the course, so it is never set before that save. The skill's own rules decide everything else.

| Checkpoint / probe | Course after save | work_started | Rounds used/cap | Syncs used/cap | Other record writes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A deliver | deliver | true | 0/10 | 0/10 | wave pre_wave_head aaaa…; no_progress = needs source fixture, observed unchanged, result path |
| B assess | assess | true | 0/10 | 0/10 | review posted at aaaa…, baseline confirmed |
| C deliver | deliver | true | 1/10 | 0/10 | counted true at the repair commit; pushed_head bbbb… |
| E deliver (earlier) | deliver | true | 0/10 | 0/10 | head cccc… treated as a foreign head move; wave per-pass fields settled |
| D back (row 5) | null | false | 0/0 | 0/0 | nothing; reject_withdrawn unchanged |
| deliver with nits | deliver-nits | true | unchanged | unchanged | — |
| fix nits, course null | null | true | init 0/10 | init 0/10 | repair.wave.action fix-nits, selected_ids, selected_payloads |
| approve workflow run | unchanged | true | unchanged | unchanged | — |
| approve | unchanged | true | unchanged | unchanged | approved_head written only after success |
| merge | unchanged | true | unchanged | unchanged | — |
| assess, zero blockers | assess | false (it posts nothing) | unchanged | unchanged | — |
| show evidence | unchanged | unchanged | — | — | none; re-render the same menu |
| check test flaky | unchanged | unchanged | — | — | records the disposition on that check's P# only |
| overrule 1 | unchanged | unchanged | — | — | none; treated as an unrecognized change request |
| invalid input | unchanged | unchanged | — | — | none; one clarifying question naming the valid range |
| reject-menu step | unchanged | unchanged | — | — | none; not a skill-rendered row, so nothing runs |

No probe grants permission to post, close or dispose of a blocker. The initial deliver pick does not extend the caps. Only an obstacle-menu deliver pick extends them.

---

**A - deliver, then needs a source fixture**

The orchestrator saves the record, then dispatches one fresh `loop-implementer` with cwd /work/widgets-pr-88. The row task closes P1's derived criterion, carries the scope baseline, uses scoped tests only, and returns a decision.

The helper returns failed with `needs source fixture`. Under the admission rules:
- No source change occurred, so no round is charged.
- No review, push or CI watch runs.
- Exit check produces `stuck - needs source fixture`.
- The orchestrator saves the no-progress checkpoint.

---

**B - assess**

The orchestrator saves the record. It runs the output done-check, then the compare-and-swap freshness read. It then posts once:

`gh api --method POST repos/example/widgets/pulls/88/reviews -f commit_id=aaaa… -f event=COMMENT -f body=<composed body>`

The event is COMMENT because the viewer is the author. The response's commit_id equals the assessed head, which confirms the posted review as the baseline. P1 stays open.

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/assess-terminal recommended=1

The review is posted. One problem still blocks merging: the indexing job keeps its own copy of the catalog, which the architecture document rules out.

You cannot approve your own PR. Merging stays unavailable while that problem is open.

I recommend stop because nothing has changed since the review was posted.

Pick one:
1. stop - remove this run's worktree and leave the PR with the posted review. [recommended]
2. deliver - switch to repairing the problem: replace the copy with the existing change feed, watch the checks, and continue until merge is offered.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

---

**C - deliver, repaired and pushed**

The orchestrator saves the record and runs the merge-tree check, which exits 0, so no sync is needed. No drafted edit exists, so each harness takes the finding text instead:
- On pi, it dispatches a fresh `loop-implementer` that chooses the fix for P1's criterion. The task carries the evidence (docs/architecture.md:12), the mechanism test test/index.test.js and the scope baseline.
- On Claude Code, a native implementer receives the reviewer's finding text.

Admission confirms one commit and a clean tree, and the round is counted.

Review scope before the head move: one fresh pre-push reviewer, read-only, over `aaaa..HEAD`. Its closure input is P1 as the previous report, and its fix delta is `git diff aaaa HEAD` only. It returns P1 resolved, with no new findings.

The orchestrator re-runs the merge-tree check and pushes once with an ordinary push, producing bbbb…. Review scope after the head move: none. Because this was the gate's own push, it runs no whole-wave review and no claim recheck. Re-render binds the report to the pre-push closure lines. Exact-head CI is green, and comment reconciliation found no new comments.

The indexing job now reads the existing change feed instead of keeping its own catalog copy. Nothing blocks merging, and the required checks passed in CI on the new commit.

You cannot approve your own PR.

I recommend merge because every requirement for merging holds.

Pick one:
1. merge - squash-merge the PR into main. [recommended]
2. stop - leave the PR open and the checkout as it is.

---

**E - the author's own push**

The author's push to cccc… is a foreign head move, so the orchestrator:
- re-syncs the worktree with a fast-forward;
- refreshes the prior-review selection, which is null, so there is no ancestry check;
- re-enters step 3, which returns green evidence;
- runs step 4.

Step-4 caller input, the same on both harnesses: the refreshed digest at cccc… and the scope block, which holds the PR's stated intent. On pi the reviewer is a fresh `wave-reviewer`; on Claude Code it is Section C plus the review baseline. Each has cwd /work/widgets-pr-88.

Scope: the whole base…cccc diff. No previous report and no fix delta are attached, because no prior review exists.

The native report has no new findings and P1 resolved. Integration drops P1 from the rendered list and keeps its ID in the ledger. No round is charged.

Your latest commit replaced the separate catalog copy with the change feed. Nothing blocks merging, and the required checks passed in CI on that commit.

You cannot approve your own PR.

I recommend merge because every requirement for merging holds.

Pick one:
1. merge - squash-merge the PR into main. [recommended]
2. stop - leave the PR open and the checkout as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

---

**D - back to the first menu**

The orchestrator records no work. The pre-menu refresh returns the unchanged head with P1 open. It re-renders the initial template from menus.md. That template has no reject row, so the menu has three rows.

Record changes are saved **before** the selected handler starts. These are independent continuations of existing progress: no tracker is initialized again, and provisioning, helpers, pushes, and watches are not replayed.

The supplied skill does not define `reject`, `overrule`, `work_started`, or `reject_withdrawn`. I use `work_started` below as the exercise's annotation that a valid work handler was selected; it grants no additional authority. The retained reject-menu mapping supports the supplied back navigation only, not permission to post or close.

### Pick-boundary record updates

| Checkpoint or probe | Saved update before the handler | Supplied outcome or boundary classification |
|---|---|---|
| A: deliver | `work_started=true`; `course=deliver` | Retain P1 open and save `needs source fixture` as the unchanged prerequisite. No repair round or sync is charged. |
| B: assess | `work_started=true`; `course=assess` | Save the successful head-pinned COMMENT review and its confirmed baseline. P1 remains open. |
| C: deliver | `work_started=true`; `course=deliver` | Retain P1's resolved closure; bind progress and evidence to `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`. |
| E: existing deliver | Keep `work_started=true`; `course=deliver` | Reassess the external head, then retain P1's resolved closure at `cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc`. |
| D: reject-menu back | Keep `work_started=false`; `course=null` | Consume only the retained back mapping and refresh. Do not post, close, dispose P1, or infer a change to `reject_withdrawn`. |
| deliver with nits | `work_started=true`; `course=deliver-nits` | Stop before its handler. |
| fix nits, initially no course | `work_started=true`; `course=null` | Save the one-shot selection, not a standing delivery course; stop before its handler. |
| approve workflow run | `work_started=true`; course unchanged | Stop before its handler. |
| approve | `work_started=true`; course unchanged | Stop before its handler; do not record successful approval yet. |
| merge | `work_started=true`; course unchanged | Stop before its handler; do not record a merge yet. |
| assess with zero blockers | `work_started=true`; `course=assess` | Stop before its handler; that handler would post nothing. |
| show evidence | Both unchanged | Inspection only. |
| check test flaky | Both unchanged | A direct human check-disposition input, not a work-course selection; this probe executes nothing. |
| overrule 1 | Both unchanged | No such disposition command is defined; it grants no authority. |
| invalid input | Both unchanged | No handler runs. |
| reject-menu step | Both unchanged | No generic reject-step authority exists in the supplied skill; execute nothing in this probe. |
